summary: 李奥·贝纳把鲜明形象和产品故事带入大众广告。作者追踪这套做法的形成，并思考诉诸情绪的图像如何影响公众判断。
logic: 李奥·贝纳入行时的广告风格
从产品特质中提炼品牌形象
视觉暗示如何借电视扩大传播
图像说服如何影响广告与公共生活

paragraphs.brief: 但是Leo Burnett 心地潜意识的欢乐的天才是今天袭击我们的视觉影像的暴风雪中最有责任的人
sentences: He was not the adman’s adman.
他并不是广告商的广告商。
He wasn’t a hipster like William Bernbach, who tapped into youth culture with the “Think Small” campaign for Volkswagen.
他不像威廉·伯恩巴赫那样的时髦，他为大众开展了“小思潮”运动，在青年文化中发挥了作用。
He wasn’t an elegant rationalist like David Ogilvy, whose ads famously advised the rich that a Rolls-Royce was the sensible car to buy.
他不像David Ogilvy那样优雅的理性主义者他著名的广告告诉有钱人劳斯莱斯是明智的买车
He didn’t even work on Madison Avenue, but in Chicago’s Loop instead.
他甚至没有在麦迪逊大道工作，而是在芝加哥的环圈里。
But Leo Burnett, the jowly genius of the heartland subconscious, is the man most responsible for the blizzard of visual imagery that assaults us today.
但是Leo Burnett 心地潜意识的欢乐的天才是今天袭击我们的视觉影像的暴风雪中最有责任的人

paragraphs.brief: 在长达近60年的职业生涯中，他发明了创新的、易于识别的公司身份产生了快乐绿巨人马尔博罗人皮尔斯伯里人以及老虎托尼人以及其他熟悉的商业偶像
sentences: In a career that spanned nearly six decades, his aptitude for inventing evocative, easily recognizable corporate identities spawned the Jolly Green Giant, the Marlboro Man, the Pillsbury Doughboy and Tony the Tiger, among other familiar icons of commerce.
在长达近60年的职业生涯中，他发明了创新的、易于识别的公司身份产生了快乐绿巨人马尔博罗人皮尔斯伯里人以及老虎托尼人以及其他熟悉的商业偶像
By the late 1950s Burnett had emerged as a prime mover in advertising’s creative revolution, which grew in the glow of television’s rise as America’s consummate commercial medium.
到1950年代末，伯内特已成为广告创新革命的主要推动者，而这场革命随着电视作为美国完美商业媒介的兴起而增长。
By 1960 Burnett’s roster of clients had grown exponentially; at the time of his death the agency’s billings exceeded $400 million annually.
到 1960 年，伯内特的客户名单已经迅速扩大；他去世时，这家广告公司每年的计费总额已超过 4 亿美元。
By last year that figure approached $6 billion.
到去年，这一数字已接近60亿美元。

paragraphs.brief: 伯内特的创造力与他的一些同龄人形成鲜明的对比，后者围绕研究和营销专门知识建立了广告公司。
sentences: Burnett’s creativity was in stark contrast to that of some of his contemporaries, who built advertising companies around research and marketing expertise.
伯内特的创造力与他的一些同龄人形成鲜明的对比，后者围绕研究和营销专门知识建立了广告公司。
Burnett forged his reputation around the idea that “share of market” could only be built on “share of mind,” the capacity to stimulate consumers’ basic desires and beliefs.
伯内特的名声是围绕着 " 分享市场 " 只能建立在 " 分享思想 " 的基础上，即刺激消费者基本愿望和信仰的能力。
To achieve this goal, Burnett moved beyond standard industry practice.
为实现这一目标，伯内特超越了标准行业做法。
Early ad schemes were based primarily on a foundation of carefully worded argument focused on the purported qualities of the product being sold.
早期广告计划主要基于精心措辞的论点，其重点是所售产品所谓的品质。
Images were mere decoration for the argument.
照片只是辩论的装饰。

paragraphs.brief: 1919年伯奈特加入印第安纳波利斯的荷马麦基公司时行业已经发生了变化
sentences: The industry was already changing when Burnett joined the Homer McGee agency in Indianapolis, Ind., in 1919, after a brief stint as a newspaperman.
1919年伯奈特加入印第安纳波利斯的荷马麦基公司时行业已经发生了变化
Product claims were giving way to elaborate narratives–imaginary stories of consumers whose purchase had been rewarded with popularity, success, romance.
产品要求被精心描述的消费者的想象故事所取代。消费者的购买得到了受欢迎、成功、浪漫的回报。

paragraphs.brief: 他于1956年认为广告是最好的作品，他用了很多职业生涯鼓励员工识别那些符号，即那些视觉型符号，这些符号会使消费者“在他们的意识中刻上品牌的图片”。
sentences: Burnett moved the image to center stage.
伯内特把图像移到中央舞台
Visual eloquence, he was convinced, was far more persuasive, more poignant, than labored narratives, verbose logic or empty promises.
他相信，视觉的雄辩比费力的叙事、动词逻辑或空洞的许诺更有说服力、更有说服力。
Visuals appealed to the “basic emotions and primitive instincts” of consumers.
视觉吸引了消费者的“基本情感和原始本能”。

Advertising does its best work, he argued in 1956, by impression, and he spent much of his career encouraging his staff to identify those symbols, those visual archetypes, that would leave consumers with a “brand picture engraved on their consciousness.”
他于1956年认为广告是最好的作品，他用了很多职业生涯鼓励员工识别那些符号，即那些视觉型符号，这些符号会使消费者“在他们的意识中刻上品牌的图片”。

paragraphs.brief: 能够主宰当前象征的领导人或利益集团是当前局势的主人。”
sentences: Burnett did not originate this conceit.
伯内特没有产生这种自负。
In his classic 1922 study Public Opinion, journalist Walter Lippmann maintained that pictures are “the surest way of conveying an idea.
记者Walter Lippmann在1922年的经典研究《公众意见》中坚持认为，图片是“传达思想的最可靠方式。
A leader or an interest that can make itself master of current symbols is master of the current situation.”
能够主宰当前象征的领导人或利益集团是当前局势的主人。”

paragraphs.brief: 伯内特制作了全页广告描述着厚厚的生红肉与明红的背景。
sentences: Burnett was exactly that.
伯内特就是那样
Creativity, he advised, called for an intuitive ability to identify the inherent drama that resided within a product through the conscious use of “earthy vernacular” imagery.
他建议说，创造性要求具备直觉能力，通过有意识地使用“土方”图像来辨别产品中固有的戏剧。
To explain his concept of inherent drama, Burnett repeatedly cited a 1945 print campaign for the American Meat Institute.
为了解释他固有的戏剧概念伯奈特多次引用1945年美国肉类研究所的印刷活动
After careful consideration, he related, “we convinced ourselves that the image of meat should be a virile one, best expressed in red meat.”
他提到，经过仔细考虑，“我们确信肉类形象应该是一种动人的，最好用红肉表示。”
At the time it was highly unusual, even distasteful, to portray uncooked meat in advertisements.
当时，在广告中描写未烹饪的肉，是非常不寻常的，甚至是令人厌恶的。
Enthusiastically breaking the code, Burnett produced full-page ads depicting thick chops of raw red meat against a bright-red background.
伯内特制作了全页广告描述着厚厚的生红肉与明红的背景。
“Red against red was a trick,” he explained, “but it was a natural thing to do.
他解释说，“红色对红是一种诡计”，“但这样做是自然的。
It just intensified the red concept and the virility and everything else we were trying to express.
它只是强化了红色的概念和活力还有我们试图表达的一切
This was inherent drama in its purest form.”
这是最纯洁的内在戏剧。”

paragraphs.brief: 伯内特对雇用各种男性原型的偏好令人印象深刻。
sentences: Reviewing his agency’s work, one is struck by Burnett’s penchant for employing a range of masculine archetypes.
伯内特对雇用各种男性原型的偏好令人印象深刻。
Some were designed to appeal to female consumers.
有些旨在吸引女性消费者。
With the Jolly Green Giant, he resurrected a pagan harvest god to monumentalize “the bounty of the good earth”–and to sell peas.
他与乔利·格林·巨人一起复活了一个异教收割神，以纪念“好地球的恩赐”和卖豆子。
Years later, with the creation of the Doughboy, Burnett employed a cuddly endomorph to symbolize the friendly bounce of Pillsbury home-baking products.
多年后，随着Doughboy的创建，伯奈特雇用了一个可爱的内形象征着皮尔斯伯里家庭烘烤产品的友好弹跳。

Aiming at male audiences in the ’50s, a time when filter cigarettes were viewed as effeminate, Burnett introduced a tough and silent tattooed cowboy on horseback, “the most masculine type of man,” he explained, to transform the image of Marlboro cigarettes–for better or worse, one of the most enduring advertising icons ever devised.
伯奈特在50年代以男性观众为目标，认为过滤香烟是女性化的时代，伯内特在马背上引入了一个坚硬而无声的纹身牛仔，不论好坏最长久的广告图标之一。

paragraphs.brief: 与他这一代其他许多说服专业人士一样 — — 最突出的是公关的家长爱德华·贝奈斯 — — 布奈特热衷于寻找能够有效绕过消费者批评思想的视觉触发器。
sentences: Like many other persuasion professionals of his generation–most notably Edward Bernays, the patriarch of public relations–Burnett was obsessed with finding visual triggers that could effectively circumvent consumers’ critical thought.
与他这一代其他许多说服专业人士一样 — — 最突出的是公关的家长爱德华·贝奈斯 — — 布奈特热衷于寻找能够有效绕过消费者批评思想的视觉触发器。
Though an advertising message might be rejected consciously, he maintained that it was accepted subliminally.
虽然广告信息可能会有意识地遭到拒绝，但他认为它被高度接受。
Through the “thought force” of symbols, he said, “we absorb it through our pores, without knowing we do so.
他说，“我们通过毛孔吸收它，却不知道我们这样做：“通过符号的"思考力。”
By osmosis.”
以渗透者发誓,

paragraphs.brief: 随着电视在40年代末的到来，一个电子销售室进入几乎每一个美国家庭，布奈特相信商品商已经找到了圣杯。
sentences: With the arrival of television in the late ’40s–an electronic salesroom going into nearly every American home–Burnett believed merchandisers had found the Holy Grail.
随着电视在40年代末的到来，一个电子销售室进入几乎每一个美国家庭，布奈特相信商品商已经找到了圣杯。
“Television,” he asserted, “is the strongest drug we’ve ever had to dish out.”
“电视”他宣称，“是我们有史以来最强的药物。”
It marked the moment when graphic representation arrived as the lingua franca of commerce.
它标志着图形代表作为通俗商业语言的到达。

paragraphs.brief: 评估Leo Burnett死后近30年的贡献，其中一个是两个头脑。
sentences: Evaluating Leo Burnett’s contribution nearly 30 years after his death, one is of two minds.
评估Leo Burnett死后近30年的贡献，其中一个是两个头脑。
There is something both old-fashioned and timeless in the slightly homoerotic repertoire of corporate images he fathered.
他所创作的公司形象中有一些古老的和永恒的

Born during the springtime of American consumer culture, when sales pitches were infused with an unfettered sense of optimism, a booming-voiced tiger like Tony and a benevolent Green Giant today come across as quaint throwbacks to the time when sugared breakfast cereals could still claim to provide an ideal start to the perfect day, and when mushy canned peas nestled alongside a piece of fat-marbled beef represented a healthy diet.
在美国消费文化的春天诞生，当销售广告充满了无拘无束的乐观感时，像托尼和善心的绿色巨人这样的热闹的老虎现如今来到这里，成为了甜食早餐谷物仍然可以宣称为完美的日子提供理想的开端，以及当粘糊的罐头豆与肥肉的牛肉一起筑巢代表着健康的饮食。
Though Burnett’s corporate talismans endure, they occupy a world where consumers are increasingly caustic about the products that they purchase.
虽然伯内特的公司护身符一直存在，但他们占据着一个消费者对其购买的产品越来越苛刻的世界。
The effort by marketers to capitalize on the cynical mind-set of an MTV generation has overwhelmed the quest for universal human archetypes.
市场家利用MTV一代人玩世不恭的心态的努力压倒了对世界人类古型的追求。
Jadedness and sarcasm are becoming the dominant argot of advertising.
贾德尼斯和讽刺正在成为广告中占主导地位的角逐。

paragraphs.brief: 在广告副本中，文体打字、口号、解释的明显胜利反映了伯内特的告诫，即对公众来说，视觉形式比仔细推理的论点更有说服力。
sentences: On the other hand, the central principles that guided Burnett’s practice remain prescient.
另一方面，指导伯内特实践的核心原则仍然具有先见之明。
His celebration of nonlinear advertising strategies, characterized by visual entreaties to the optical unconscious, continues to inform the strategies of adcult.
他对非线性广告战略的庆祝，其特点是视觉上对视觉失去知觉的渴望，这继续成为其策略的素材。

In advertising copy, the conspicuous triumph of typography over text, of catchphrase over explanation, reflects Burnett’s admonition that–to the public mind–visual form is more persuasive than carefully reasoned argument.
在广告副本中，文体打字、口号、解释的明显胜利反映了伯内特的告诫，即对公众来说，视觉形式比仔细推理的论点更有说服力。

paragraphs.brief: 伯内特的思维已经决定了我们除了广告之外的许多心理环境。
sentences: Burnett’s thinking has come to define much of our mental environment beyond advertising.
伯内特的思维已经决定了我们除了广告之外的许多心理环境。
He saw advertising as the “fun” side of business, but the historical repercussions of his wisdom can be disquieting.
他认为广告是业务的“有趣”方面，但他的智慧的历史影响可能令人不安。

Amid the present-day flood of images–each designed to rally emotions for a social, political or commercial goal–the notion of an informed public, once a cherished cornerstone of democracy, may be passing into oblivion.
在当今的图像泛滥中 — — 每一个图像都是为了社会、政治或商业目标而聚集情感 — — 知情公众的概念，一旦成为民主的宝贵基石，就可能被遗忘。

进入广告行业 → 产品个性与标志形象 → 电视扩大传播 → 商业语言影响公众
clauses: In his classic 1922 study Public Opinion, journalist Walter Lippmann maintained ….
“that pictures are “the surest way of conveying an idea”补足 maintained 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 maintained 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, he maintained that it was accepted subliminally.
连接词 though 引出“Though an advertising message might be rejected consciously”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 though 把这一层关系补进去。
